steps.text: 33 hours before the Kjerag Catastrophe

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Instruments, check. Terminal battery, check. Pen ink and paper, check... coffee, check!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: It's all-nighter time—

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Whoa!
A rustling sound coming from a corner gives Elena a fright. Only then does she realize that she is not the only person in the observation room.
A human figure crawls out of the pile of waste paper by the instruments.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Oh... it's you, Elena.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: (Yawns) I thought some great scientist was pulling an all-nighter in an effort to win the Max Prize...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: C-Carolin?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: You remember me?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Of course I remember the rising star of the Energy Section, the youngest researcher ever to join our ranks.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I-I'm flattered...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I thought you had already left. The schedule said I was supposed to be the one on observation duty today—

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Heh, like the schedule's ever meant anything—I wouldn't have been sleeping here for two straight weeks if it did.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: No wonder I've hardly seen you ever since I came to the station...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Must be tough.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: How does it feel to be back?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Coming back to Rhine Lab.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: You were the first person I thought of when they started recruiting for the observation station project, but I thought you would turn it down.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Honestly, it wasn't an easy decision.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: At the end of the day, though, the company gave me a valuable opportunity. Besides, the achievements of Rhine Lab itself have never been in question.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I still think my time at Rhine Lab was the closest I've ever been to achieving my dreams.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: And I have to admit... even Ferdinand was a great researcher, if nothing else.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Indeed. He has a mind for physics, so let him do what he does best.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: You know, he's stopped messing with other researchers since he got out of prison, and has been spending all his time on research.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: I think there's going to be a new Director of Energy before long... maybe she's standing in front of me now.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: No no no no no no, you've got to be kidding me!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I just wanted to get a closer look...
Elena looks up and sees the sky obscured by snow through the observation's clear dome.
She hates this feeling.
Just like she hates her family's backwards traditions and beliefs, all the things in her way that have nothing to do with science itself.
She believes that science should be pure, ever-advancing, solving questions about Terra one at a time...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: This observation station is an invaluable opportunity.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I only want to focus on my research, maybe push a little further than the boundaries of existing knowledge, if I can.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Boundaries, huh... this is the closest place there is.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Say, have you heard the legend of Kjerag?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Legend? What legend?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: This land has not suffered a Catastrophe for a thousand years, thanks to the protection of their god.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Well, every country once attributed unusual phenomena to the 'gods'.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Kjerag just held onto this tradition longer because of its isolation.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Yet it is indeed true that Kjerag has not suffered a Catastrophe for a thousand years.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: It's certainly unusual... but there must be a reason.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Maybe the high elevation makes it difficult for Originium particles to converge, or—

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: A Feranmut?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Come on, I'm being serious!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I know there are legends about the Feranmuts, ancient beings the size of mountains that turn into mountains and rivers after death.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: First off, there are no confirmed accounts proving the existence of Feranmuts. Besides, if these beings did exist, where did they find the energy to sustain their biological activities?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Why bring this up, anyway?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Just something that occurred to me while we were chatting.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Well, that's enough gabbing. You can rest, I'll take over observations for the night.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Really? But you've done a bunch of night shifts in a row—

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: It's not like my circadian rhythm can get any more messed up. And chatting with you woke me up.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: If I recall correctly, there are still some bugs to iron out with the power supply to the high-energy particle beam?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Wow, y-you know about that?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Get some rest and put that brain of yours to better use.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Well, I guess I'll take you up on the offer! Thank you so much!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I'll buy you some fins and chips from that Victorian restaurant that just opened at the foot of the mountain when you have time!

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: Please don't, no Victorian wants to have to enjoy authentic Victorian cuisine in a foreign land.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Hehe... Kjerag cheese fondue, then?

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: That sounds great.
It is another deep and quiet night in Kjerag. The ancient land slumbers, and lamps give way to stars.
The sleeping snowy mountains may seem wondrous to the uninitiated, though most who live on this land have gotten used to this sight.
Few look up at the sky on a night like this.

steps.name: Carolin
steps.text: What's that...?!
Both her eyes and the instruments capture the strange light that cut across the night sky.
Like a sign from the heavens.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: It appears that Carolin was an accomplished, intelligent young researcher with a bright future.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: This project is very important to both Rhine Lab and Columbia. The recruiting process was extremely selective.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We have yet to find any irregularities in her records and communication logs.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: She was originally from Victoria?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: I am unable to provide any private information. That would be a violation of Rhine Lab's privacy policy, and basic human rights.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: We can only provide information about her time at Rhine Lab, unless your government officially presses charges of espionage.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Of course. I was just asking.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Her application material was very comprehensive, with every shift and fieldwork experience documented meticulously...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Here, it seems she even requested a field survey task for herself.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Collecting information about Kjerag's geography concurrently with her scientific research?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: She has been a diligent researcher, highly rated at Rhine Lab, and a model student when she was at school.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Such scientists are not usually involved in the kind of trouble that we currently face.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Yet, at this point, we have no information or clue as to the whereabouts of Carolin.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Believe it or not, we are even more eager to find Carolin than you are.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: There are many things at stake. Rhine Lab's reputation, the security of the research data, potential breach of our management system, the mutual trust and partnership between us, and...

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: ...And Kjerag's development.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Are you speaking as a member of the Scientific Ethics Consensus Committee?

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: Please don't misunderstand. Though it might sound a little condescending, I have the highest respect for what Karlan Trade is doing.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: After all, the courage to reach beyond one's comfort zone is the most important quality in a scientist.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Not just in scientists.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: There is a saying in Kjerag, 'Black burdenbeasts are bad burdenbeasts.'

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: They jump their fences and run into the snowfields. Herders who go into the fields following their tracks never return.

steps.name: Silence
steps.text: They die?

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: That's what 'go into the snowfields and never return' usually means in Kjerag.
One by one, pages are reviewed and placed on the table—Carolin's notes and actions turn into a tiny pile of papers.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: But where did the black burdenbeasts go? It's the same question, in the end.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Perhaps they led the herders into the mountains, getting lost in the forests and freezing to death at night.
Another page is read and placed on the table.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Or perhaps...
Gnosis puts the last page down.
White upon white, like snowflakes falling on frozen cliffs.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: They simply found a new source of water, a new haven.

steps.name: Gnosis
steps.text: Can you at least tell me where exactly she carried out her fieldwork?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I can't. The observation data are badly corrupted. I can't recover the original data from the port...
Stacks of documents and mugs with dried coffee stains sit quietly on the table.
An error tone signifies failure of the data restoration, causing their hearts to sink once more.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There are ID records of all entries and exits, no message left behind in the dorms or labs...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: The main security camera malfunctioned, while the two to the sides of the lab didn't capture anything...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: It seems like too much of a coincidence. Could Carolin really have...?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: No. Everyone else might assume she's a spy, but I can't let bias cloud my judgment. I already requested access permissions from Director Muelsyse to get to the bottom of things...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Knock, knock. Who's been up all night?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: D-Director Muelsyse?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Surprised to see me?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I hear you haven't been back to the dorms for two straight nights... are you still searching for the data that disappeared?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There is little doubt that the observation logs were altered, although we're not sure who did it, or why.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There is reason to believe that the overwritten data hold a crucial clue...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hm... but...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Never mind. I brought you a li'l snacky. Can't work on an empty stomach, after all.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Thank you. What is this?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You've never had it? Kjerag cheese pastries with sugar frosting and berry jam. It was all the rage at the station a while back.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I heard people talking about it and had planned on trying them out the next time I went down the mountain for fondue, but I've been too busy investigating special energy sources unique to Kjerag.
Elena picks up a pastry. It's dried up on the outside, but the cheese and jam inside remain moist after being heated.
The sound of running water ceases, and Muelsyse sits down by her side with two clean mugs in hand.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Mind if I sip a cuppa joe with you?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Not at all.
Fresh coffee fills the mugs, drenching the air in its aroma.
The sound of machines operating is clearly audible at this late hour. A massive window on the wall displays the stars in Kjerag's night sky, deep and boundless as always.
The atmosphere in the room relaxes. Elena lifts her mug after a moment of hesitation.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Midnight coffee in the lab. Brings back memories.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: You used to stay up late too?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Who doesn't, in our line of work?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Even when I was a student, it felt like I had more coffee than blood in veins for finals—

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Haha... Looks like everyone's been there before.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Working at night's more efficient, after all.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Yes. Night is quiet. Makes it easier to focus.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: I used to write one paper while dictating the summary of another using an audio recorder, when I was really busy.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: That way, I get to make progress on both at the same time. Crazy, when I think back to it...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Oh yeah! Audio recorder!

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Huh? Audio? Where are you going?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Surveillance audio recordings!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Surveillance camera, credentials... the time is... 3:19 am...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Didn't you say the cameras didn't capture what was happening at the lab table?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Yes... but it might have captured sound from the equipment.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Listen to this... a lot of instruments operating. This ticking sound should be the audio sensor.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: The frequency that it plays back is directly connected to graphing. We can use this frequency to recreate—excuse me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Need a pen and paper? Here you go.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Oh, thanks.
Pen tip rubs against paper. The time they spend around the instruments have made researchers intimately familiar with data.
She enters the numbers that she copied down into the computer, then...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: There...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: This is the hidden data.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Lemme take a look-see...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Looks like a small earthquake occurred on Mount Karlan the morning of the day before the Catastrophe.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: No... not an earthquake. It was an impact of some kind.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: As if something fell from the sky into the mountains of Kjerag.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: And then... came Kjerag's first Catastrophe.
Outside the wide windows of the observation station, the mountains of Kjerag seem to reflect a translucent blue under the moon.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Did Carolin go looking for this extraterrestrial object?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But why would she do it all on her own?

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: She's never abandoned her post like this. She must have found something...

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: We might be able to find her, if we figure out where that thing fell!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Which we can calculate from the wave frequency of the sound of impact!

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: Director Muelsyse, we...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The Vine-Bead Court isn't about to investigate on our behalf.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Strictly speaking, we shouldn't get any more involved in any of this stuff. The most we can do is to report this to Component Control.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: But Carolin might be in danger...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You know that's not your job.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You're not exactly close to Carolin. Bluntly, whatever happens to her is none of your business.
Muelsyse finishes her cold coffee in silence.
Frowning at the bitter taste, she takes a piece of pastry and puts it in her mouth, speaking as she chews.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...But.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sometimes, I kinda think the most important quality in a scientist is courage... maybe even recklessness.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You're a sharp kiddo. Got a knack for finding rhythm in music.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Makes for a good dancer. I wouldn't wanna tie you up, gotta let you move around free.

steps.name: Elena
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: This conversation never happened. Nobody tried to talk you out of it, nobody told you what you can or can't do...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: As for this late night snack... you took it from the shared fridge yourself, didn't you?
